## Judgment

### Expected-drift set

`modules/core/security.nix` is reached by every NixOS host through both the
workstation and server profiles, so dropping `enableSSHSupport` and changing
the gpg-agent cache TTLs drifts all four. `modules/tools/ssh-tpm-agent.nix`
adds a session variable on sweet16 and petunia only. `cert-check.sh` is not
evaluated by any configuration and contributes no drift.

Expected: all four NixOS hosts drift; the standalone groot HM configurations
do not move.

### Actual vs expected

Matches: sweet16, petunia, avina and hermes drift; groot@dualie and
groot@forge byte-identical; groot@rk3588 N/A (aarch64).

### Verified before deploying, not after

The replacement path was proven while the old one was still live:

- A Vault certificate was issued against `~/.ssh/tpm/id_ecdsa_personal.pub`
  via `ssh-client-signer/sign/adminrole`, principal `root`, 8h. The CA is the
  same one already trusted by the fleet.
- ssh-tpm-agent picks the certificate up from its key directory unprompted and
  offers it as a separate ECDSA-CERT identity beside the bare key.
- With the agent holding *only* that key and cert, `root@` publickey
  authentication succeeds on sweet16, petunia, avina and hermes — the whole
  deploy path.
- `ddukes@petunia`, `groot@avina` and `groot@hermes` also authenticate on the
  TPM key alone, exercising the enrolled `authorized_keys` entries.

An earlier failure of this test was my own error: `IdentitiesOnly=yes` with no
`IdentityFile` suppresses agent identities entirely. Removing it showed the
certificate being offered and accepted.

### Why this is safe to remove gpg-agent's SSH role

Neither consumer of the old agent depends on it. `~/.ssh/id_ed25519` carries
no passphrase and Gitea resolves it through `IdentitiesOnly` against the
default identity *files*, never the agent. GitHub is HTTPS via
`gh auth git-credential`.

### GPG cache

Raised from 8h/24h to a week for `default-cache-ttl` and `max-cache-ttl`. The
practical bound is gpg-agent's own lifetime, which ends with the login
session, so this is "once per session" rather than a literal week. It settles
the original re-prompting complaint for GPG without the TPM-backed signing
work, which is deferred.

### Still outstanding

`~/.ssh/id_ed25519` remains enrolled everywhere and readable on disk without a
passphrase — the exposure TPM sealing exists to remove. Retiring it is the
next step and is now unblocked, since the deploy path no longer depends on its
certificate.
